newsitem.title: CUBA: Che Guevara's bones arrive in Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Che Guevara's bones arrive in Cuba.

text.p: The last remains of the legendary leftist guerrilla Ernesto "Che" Guevara arrived in Cuba on Saturday, almost 30 years after he was captured and shot in October 1967 while leading an abortive rebel uprising in Bolivia.
President Fidel Castro was present at a reception ceremony at San Antonio de los Banos airbase about 20 miles (30 km) south of Havana, where Guevara's remains were flown from Bolivia.
Guevara's remains were brought to Cuba along with those of three Cuban guerrilla comrades unearthed from the same mass grave near Vallegrande in Bolivia last week by a team of Latin American experts.
A Cuban guard of honor including Che's old comrade-in-arms Commander Ramiro Valdez accompanied the remains on the flight back aboard a Cuban plane to the Communist-ruled island.

An Argentine-born doctor, Guevara served as Castro's right-hand man during the rebel struggle that brought Castro to power in 1959. He became one of Cuba's most revered heroes and was an icon for a generation of leftists around the world.
